---
title: "Serving Worker republication"
description: "How production promotion republishes the Workers that already serve roadmap, learn, teach, nova, tools and lms, how one approval admits a round, how the fleet summary fails on stale apps, and how to stop, retry or roll one back."
updatedAt: '2026-11-26'
audience: developers
---

Some native Workers already serve production traffic through the apex gateway
mount and their own hosts. A production promotion must reach them as well, or a
dependency fix (for example a React Server Components advisory) stays merged but
unshipped. `serving-workers-production.yaml` closes that gap.

| App | Worker | Public origins | Sealed artifact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| roadmap | `tuturuuu-roadmap` | `tuturuuu.com/roadmap` | `roadmap-worker-<sha>` |
| learn | `tuturuuu-learn` | `learn.tuturuuu.com`, `tuturuuu.com/learn` | `learn-cutover-production-<sha>` |
| teach | `tuturuuu-teach` | `teach.tuturuuu.com`, `tuturuuu.com/teach` | `teach-cutover-production-<sha>` |
| nova | `tuturuuu-nova` | `tuturuuu.com/nova` | `nova-cutover-production-<sha>` |
| tools | `tuturuuu-tools` | `tools.tuturuuu.com`, `tuturuuu.com/tools` | `tools-cutover-<sha>` |
| lms | `tuturuuu-lms` | `tuturuuu.com/lms` | `lms-worker-<sha>` |

`scripts/ci/serving-workers-apps.mjs` holds this table. Each app also needs an
`admitted` entry in `productionPublicationPolicy` (`tuturuuu.ci.ts`); a `held`
entry or a `productionAppExclusions` line keeps `plan` from selecting that app
and stops the publisher.

## Flow

On every push to `production`:

1. `plan` runs on the production branch only, with no environment, so it never
   waits for an approval. It first refuses to start a publish round on top of an
   unacknowledged RED fleet summary (see below). It then reads each app's public
   `/api/build-info` and selects every app that does not serve the production
   SHA yet, so a failed or skipped earlier promotion is retried by the next one.
2. Each selected app's own workflow runs through `workflow_call` at the exact
   production SHA and seals its production artifact. Its qualification-only
   `native` jobs do not run on the production ref.
3. One `publish` matrix job calls `serving-worker-publish.yaml` once per
   selected app. Every leg needs every build, so all legs wait on the
   `cloudflare-release-production` reviewer gate at the same moment, and one
   approval (one `pending_deployments` call for the run) admits the whole round.
   A build that failed or was skipped leaves its leg to fail at the artifact
   download, and the fleet summary reports that app as `FAILED`.
   `serving-worker-publish.yaml` runs one app at a time per
   `serving-worker-publish-<app>` concurrency group. It restores the sealed
   archive, reruns the seal verifier and converts the archive's own emitted
   config to cf Build Output with `void-cf-output.mjs`. Cron triggers stay
   configured on the Worker and are never part of a version, so they are left
   out of the uploaded config and checked against the live schedules instead.
4. The publisher refuses a split deployment (another rollout is in progress)
   and any source that is not a fast-forward of the live build, and skips when
   live already serves the SHA.
5. `void-cf-publisher.mjs publish --strict` uploads one version with no traffic
   and rejects any binding that differs from the serving version.
6. The candidate is staged at 0% beside the serving version and smoked through
   the `Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides` header, including through the
   apex gateway mount, once the override reaches the candidate (deployment
   writes take a few seconds to propagate). Build-info must report the SHA on every origin, each
   probe must match the serving status and redirect, and the page's scripts and
   stylesheets must return 200. Afterwards the serving version is restored
   alone and must read back steadily, so nothing changes for readers yet.
7. `void-cf-publisher.mjs assign --expect-current <serving>` moves 100% of
   traffic only while the captured version still serves, then waits for the
   public build-info to report the SHA. On failure the captured version is
   restored, but only over a deployment this run wrote; another writer's
   deployment is left in place and recorded.

Every step lands in the `serving-<app>-publication-<sha>-<run>-<attempt>`
artifact, retained 90 days. The receipt (schema 2) records:
- the `preimage` (the serving deployment and version, that version's upload
  message, the newest uploaded version, and the live build SHA);
- the artifact name and digest, and the run identity;
- the candidate's build-info and the smoke failures;
- the `rollbackVersion` that served before;
- `latestIsNotServing`. Cloudflare's `/settings` and `/secrets` writes build on
  the newest uploaded version, not the serving one. After
  a smoke failure that left serving in place, change a secret only after
  checking this flag.

The candidate's build-info must report `environment: production` and a
`production` or `main` ref when those fields exist. A build made without the
`PLATFORM_BUILD_*` variables reports `local` and fails the smoke.

## Fleet summary

`fleet-summary` runs after every enabled round with no environment and no
Cloudflare token; it uses only the run's read-only `github.token`. It reads
`scripts/ci/production-fleet.mjs`, which has one entry for every directory
under `apps/`:

| Class | Meaning | Verdicts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | Published by this workflow | `FRESH`; `STALE`, `UNKNOWN` or `FAILED` fail the run |
| `special` | Its own reviewed publisher (web, gateway, tasks, Meet, Cron, ...) | `FRESH` or `FRESH-EQUIVALENT` (the planner's affected-path rules see no input change since the live build); `STALE` or `UNKNOWN` fail the run, `PENDING` does not; no public identity is reported as `UNVERIFIED` |
| `held` | A deliberate hold (Lettin, Parley, Colab, Track, Mind, Drive, Contacts and Whiteboards) | `HELD`, reported as held by policy |
| `manual` | No automatic publisher yet; carries the slice that automates it and an `until` date | `MANUAL`; `EXPIRED` after the date, which fails the run |
| `inactive` | Paused or not a Worker | `INACTIVE` |

`scripts/ci/production-fleet.test.mjs` fails when a new app directory has no
entry, or when the fleet's holds disagree with `productionAppExclusions` and the
`held` entries of `productionPublicationPolicy`. The report is retained as
`fleet-freshness-<sha>-<run>-<attempt>`.

A RED summary rolls nothing back and does not undo apps already promoted in the
round. The next full publish round that starts after the RED summary completes
stops in `plan` until one of these happens (a round still awaiting approval
when the next one starts is not consulted; the next round's own summary covers
the whole fleet):

- The release owner sets the repository variable `FLEET_SUMMARY_ACK` to the
  RED run's id. Only the release owner sets it, as a recorded decision.
- The cause is fixed: dispatch the affected app alone (single-app dispatches
  are not gated), then re-run the RED run's `fleet-summary` job. When it
  passes, the gate opens.

Single-app dispatches are partial rounds: their run name
contains `(partial` and their summary job is `fleet-summary-partial`, so they
never clear or set the gate. An auto app that serves the SHA counts as fresh
even when this run's receipt for it failed, so a re-run summary after a
single-app fix passes. The summary waits up to 10 minutes for the pipelines that
publish `special` apps (for example `vercel-production.yaml` for tasks and Meet)
to finish. An app whose pipeline is still running after that is `PENDING` (not
RED) only while that run is at most 45 minutes old and the pipeline's latest
completed production push run succeeded. A `PENDING` summary passes and clears
the gate; if the pipeline then fails, the next round's summary reports the app
RED. Re-run the summary when the pipeline finishes to confirm it sooner. The
age counts from the run attempt's `run_started_at`, which includes queued time,
so a run queued behind earlier production pushes can turn `UNKNOWN`. That fails
safe: re-run the summary after the pipeline finishes, or acknowledge the run. A
stuck pipeline, or one whose previous production run did not succeed, is
`UNKNOWN`, which is RED. A summary that times out or is cancelled blocks the
next round like a failure. Receipts from re-run attempts are merged by keeping
the latest attempt per app.

Each publish leg waits for its own sealed build to succeed. Failed builds
and restore failures are RED. The summary reports a coordinator-declined
leg as `COORDINATOR-SKIPPED` and shows the build it observed live.

## Stop, retry and roll back

- **Stop.** Set the repository variable `SERVING_WORKERS_PUBLICATION` to
  anything other than `enabled`. New runs build and publish nothing. A job reads
  the variable when it starts, so cancel the workflow run to stop a publisher
  that is already running. Cancelling leaves the current step as it is, which
  can be a 0% stage or a just-assigned candidate; restore the receipt's
  `rollbackVersion` as described below.
- **Retry one app.** Dispatch `serving-workers-production.yaml` on `production`
  with that app. It rebuilds only if the app does not serve the SHA yet.
- **Catch up an off-branch live build.** When the live build is not an
  ancestor of the production SHA, the publisher refuses. An ACKed catch-up
  dispatches with `supersede` set to that exact live SHA; the receipt records
  the superseded build. A live build that already contains the source (a newer
  build) is never replaced.
- **Roll back.** Read `rollbackVersion` from the receipt and run
  `cf workers deployments create --worker <worker> --strategy percentage --versions '[{"version_id":"<rollbackVersion>","percentage":100}]'`.
  Routes, custom domains, schedules and the gateway are never changed by this
  flow.

## Activation

Every enabled run publishes each admitted app whose live build differs from
the pinned production SHA, so any regression in that SHA ships with it. Before
setting `SERVING_WORKERS_PUBLICATION=enabled`, confirm the pinned production SHA
has no known regression for an admitted app, for example by smoking each app's
candidate from that SHA at 0%. While a pinned production SHA carries a known
regression, keep the variable unset or move that app to `held` in
`productionPublicationPolicy` until a fixed SHA is pinned.

## Credentials

Enable `SERVING_WORKERS_PUBLICATION` only while the round's token exists.
Without it, every publish leg stops at "Cloudflare deploy credentials are not
configured" before any Cloudflare write, and the round ends RED.

`SERVING_WORKERS_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` is a per-round environment secret on
`cloudflare-release-production`:
- A mint child mints it at round start, scoped to Workers Scripts edit and read
  on the production account only. Zone permissions are added only when an app's
  routes need them, and that needs a per-round ACK.
- It expires at the end of the round plus two hours.
- It is revoked after the round, and custody is deleted only after a
  verification call returns 401.
- No standing or weekly token exists, and CI holds no token that can mint
  others.

Between rounds the secret is absent and `SERVING_WORKERS_PUBLICATION` is
`disabled`. The publisher runs in the
called workflow `serving-worker-publish.yaml`, and a called workflow reads a
secret, environment ones included, only when its caller hands secrets over, so
the `publish` matrix job in `serving-workers-production.yaml` sets
`secrets: inherit`. A publish job without it starts with an empty token and
stops at "Cloudflare deploy credentials are not configured" before any
Cloudflare write; `scripts/ci/serving-workers-workflow.test.mjs` guards it. `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and
`NOVA_ABUSE_GUARD_FAMILIES` are repository variables. Rotate the token through
the token ledger and set it with `gh secret set --env` from standard input so it
is never printed.

## Local release

When CI runners are unavailable, mirror the app's own artifact job on a trusted
host at the production SHA, pack the archive the same way, then run the same
publisher with the same environment:

```bash
node scripts/ci/serving-workers.mjs restore <app> <sha> <artifact-dir> <absent-output-dir>
SERVING_WORKERS_PUBLICATION=enabled node scripts/ci/serving-workers.mjs publish <app> <sha> <output-dir>
```

The roadmap seal and its verifier need Linux `/proc`; on macOS run them in a
Linux container, and pack archives with `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1` so macOS metadata
files do not enter the sealed tree. A shallow checkout drops the roadmap commit
metrics, so build roadmap from full history.
